system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s draft should **not** be accepted as a package. Its broad disclosure, knowledge and limitation clauses could substantially reduce the value of the warranties, while several identified risks remain unresolved. The Disclosure Letter describes the data-room position as at **22 September 2026**; request current evidence before signing.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **AUD 4.8m (20% of price)**. | A materially higher cap; open at **100% of price**, with any compromise assessed alongside security and the final risk allocation. | **Counter.** A 20% cap gives limited recourse on a AUD 24m acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 per claim; AUD 250,000 aggregate **excess-only** basket. | Lower thresholds and a **tipping basket** (all qualifying loss recoverable once crossed), with related claims aggregated. | **Counter.** The proposed structure leaves the first AUD 250,000 of valid loss with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**; Seller seeks to apply time limits to all Claims by default. | At least **24–36 months** for general warranties; separate, longer periods for other claim categories. | **Counter.** Some breaches may not emerge within 18 months, and one default period must not extinguish distinct remedies. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limit. | A separate **100%-of-price cap** and longer survival for capacity, ownership and authority warranties. | **Reject.** The Buyer is paying for all shares and needs full recourse if title or authority fails. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to **all Claims of any nature**. | An express carve-out for fraud and intentional dishonesty from every cap, threshold, time limit, exclusion and exclusive-remedy provision. | **Insist.** General “all Claims” wording must not shield fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only **specific, fairly disclosed** matters, with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope, should qualify identified warranties. | **Reject blanket disclosure.** Mere availability of a document is not meaningful allocation of a disclosed risk. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer/advisers or discoverable from data room or public records. | Delete constructive/deemed knowledge; at most, narrowly define actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, without adviser imputation. | **Reject as drafted.** It could defeat claims based on facts no decision-maker actually knew. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied upon written counterparty consent. No final consent or evidence of clause 11.3 conditions is supplied. | A **Completion condition** requiring effective written consent and satisfaction or waiver of all associated conditions, on terms acceptable to Buyer. | **Insist on evidence before Completion.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Repay from Seller proceeds **at Completion** under a verified payout letter, with contemporaneous release documents and a clear discharge process. | **Reject post-Completion release alone.** Debt-free/cash-free pricing requires a clean debt and security exit. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller funds or price adjusts for bonuses **and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs**, with amounts and payment responsibility itemised. | **Fix funds flow.** The Buyer should not inherit an unpriced Completion-triggered cost. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 is open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Evidence of cleared payment and effective transfer before Completion, plus a **specific indemnity covering all resulting IP-title losses and cure costs**, backed by retention if needed. | **Expand protection.** Paying the invoice alone may not establish or cure ownership of the Project Materials. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said not to be material; access, scope and notification status remain unknown. | Completed investigation, preservation and remediation evidence, legal notification assessment, pre-Completion updates and a specific indemnity for this incident. | **Do not accept a no-loss assumption.** The disclosed facts do not yet establish exposure or its absence. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Contracts and timing analysed together; identify whether each obligation is accrued, unavoidable or terminable, then reflect any pre-Completion liability in price/debt-like items. | **Reserve classification.** The AUD 330,000 aggregate cannot be dismissed without its terms and timing. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | Limitations and exclusive remedy apply to all Claims. | Express separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, debt and price adjustments, and fraud; no unintended cross-application. | **Redraft definitions and priority clauses.** A global limitation could nullify specially negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Verify issued capital, beneficial ownership, options/convertibles, encumbrances and transfer authority; obtain appropriate registers, searches, releases and Completion deliverables. | **Do not rely on the register alone.** It is evidence of registered holding, not conclusive proof of unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | Separate tax covenant/indemnity with survival tied to applicable assessment periods; robust IP ownership and infringement warranties plus targeted Ironquay protection. | **Keep open.** These exposures have different discovery periods and potential losses from ordinary warranty claims. |

**Priority before signing:** resolve Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and the incident with updated evidence, and reconcile the bonuses and Sandbar commitments to the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics.
=== END ADVICE ===
